heard: A dead star is building a new planet from its own ashes. In 1999, the Hubble Space Telescope recorded 100 mystery spectral lines around a cooling white dwarf. For 25 years, these chemical fingerprints remained a total mystery that scientists could not decipher. Using modern databases, University of Warwick researchers recently identified the mystery element as niobium. Niobium is a heavy metal forged only during the violent death throes of a dying star. The metal is being stripped from a Jupiter-sized planet orbiting just 3.7 million miles from the star. This gas giant is a rare second-generation world, born from the ruins of a destroyed solar system. It orbits through a comet-like trail of dust, reclaiming the ashes of its past life.
